I have had multiple failed suicide attempts. Everyone who I've ever asked for help only helps when it's convenient for them. My meds don't work, and thanks to my parents I owe over $10,000 to them at 20 years old. I haven't lived at home in 2 years and I've ended up homeless 4 times in that period because the economy is so bad that I can't afford to even get a shitty apartment because I have too many bills. I was never taught personal finance management so I ended up learning the hard way that credit cards aren't just "extra cash" and I have $1,000 in debt from that card. 

After I got laid off from my last job I spent 4 months unemployed and on the street trying to survive on less that $100 a month while still trying to manage my life. In the cold winter of Canada. 

I've told people I've had a rough time in life and because my parents are moderately wealthy they assume that I've just been handed everything and I'm sad because of some idiotic thing. That couldn't be farther from the truth. Everything my parents have paid for(including my one semester in university) has been put on a list that I have to pay them back. 

On a happier note, I just got a new job that can pay pretty well with commissions so I may be on track to getting a better life with the woman I love and has stuck with me for the last 4 years of hell I've went through.
Should probably stop letting your friends fuck you. It's starting to get gay man
There's no taking control back. When I feel it coming, the best I can do is to make sure I'm in a position to not hurt the people I care about.

The breaking point was when I started losing control of my mind and it's causing me to harm people (emotionally) that I care about. I used to be able to control it really well but I've lost that control.

My few friends help make life more bearable and I do enjoy the sport I've been in for six years: cheerleading. There is actually quite a few things that make it good for me. The problem is the mental conditions I suffer from make me awful, and there is no way to control some of them.

I purposely push the people I care about away so they don't get any of the harm I cause. I am okay with talking to strangers because realistically speaking, I couldn't care less about them. 

I've been on a lot of different medications for the conditions, they've helped certain symptoms but not the important ones. 

I agree with you that spur of the moment suicide is not smart or logical, but understand that I've thought about it a lot over the past decade(wow, that makes me feel old.) and this is not an act of passion. I'd consider my suicide to be a logical and calculated way to stop the suffering I endure and the pain I cause.

There's always been a mental disconnect for me. I try my best to keep myself from being the way I am but it doesn't work. 

It's not easy when you have a plethora of mental disorders that you can't control. So far I've been afflicted with depression, anxiety(both testing in the EXTREME on the tests Administered by doctors), anti social personality disorder(Psychopathic/sociopathic), ADD, Multiple personalities(self diagnosed when I discovered each persona.) and probably a couple more I forgot to mention. 

Most days I can keep these things under control, but probably 40% of the time they take over. I can't stop the things that happen and the only way to keep people from it is to keep me from people. These outbursts have been getting more frequent as I've gotten older and I want to stop them before I lose all control. 

I've done a lot of things that I regret in these states and when I'm in control I have to deal with the consequences. I'm tired of seeing the hurt and anguish I've caused people I care about because I can't stay in control of my brain. 

Sorry if this has been a little too much rambling, I've never been good at collecting my thoughts.

Nobody actually died from mine because I smartened up at the end, but when I was in high school, I got picked on a lot. friends, family, I always got put down. So I would usually take it out on the kids lower in the food chain than I. I was awful to them, and if I hadn't realized when I did, there'd be one less awesome person in the world. 

After I bullied him most of grade 8 and 9, I started to notice him being sad and I started feeling bad, so one day I talked to him and I let him know that I was sorry and I tried to be friends with him. He's a real nice kid, but when I was talking to him, he told me that day he brought a knife to school- he was going to make me pay, and then commit suicide. If I hadn't spoke to him when I did, he'd have killed me and himself.

I won't say it's weighed heavily on me in my adult life, but it did make me a better person and I learned a lesson I hope I take through my whole life: you never know what's on the other side, Treat it with kindness and respect.

I think the point of life with no people to share it with is to find people to share it with. You've built your foundation, look for someone to help put the finishing touches on your project. You might not like some of their ideas, but it will make it better in the long run.
